text:
Predicates:
Employee(x) ::: x is an employee.
Schedule(x, y) ::: x schedules a meeting with y.
Appear(x, y) ::: x appears in y.
Customer(y) ::: y is a customer.
LunchInCompany(x) ::: x has lunch in the company.
LunchAtHome(x) ::: x has lunch at home.
WorkRemotely(x) ::: x works remotely from home.
InCountry(x, y) ::: x is in country y.
Manager(x) ::: x is a manager.
Premises:
∀x ∀y (Employee(x) ∧ Customer(y) ∧ Schedule(x, y) → Appear(x, company)) ::: All employees who schedule a meeting with their customers will appear in the company today.
∀x (LunchInCompany(x) → ∃y (Customer(y) ∧ Schedule(x, y))) ::: Everyone who has lunch in the company schedules meetings with their customers.
∀x (Employee(x) → (LunchInCompany(x) ⊕ LunchAtHome(x))) ::: Employees will either have lunch in the company or have lunch at home.
∀x (LunchAtHome(x) → WorkRemotely(x)) ::: If an employee has lunch at home, then he/she is working remotely from home.
∀x ∀y (Employee(x) ∧ InCountry(x, y) ∧ ¬y=company → WorkRemotely(x)) ::: All employees who are in other countries work remotely from home.
¬∃x (Manager(x) ∧ WorkRemotely(x)) ::: No managers work remotely from home.
(Manager(james) ∧ Appear(james, company)) ⊕ ¬(Manager(james) ∨ Appear(james, company)) ::: James is either a manager and appears in the company today or neither a manager nor appears in the company today.
Conclusion:
LunchInCompany(james) ::: James has lunch in the company.
